note: one declarative source for every platform verdict supports. read by extension/src/extract/sites.ts, which derives url parsing, review page urls, the content script matches, the bridge allowlist, and the thumbnail host allowlist from it. adding a platform is an entry here plus a rules file in extension/src/extract/rules and its line in extension/src/extract/bundledRules.ts, and bundledRules.test.ts checks all three against each other so a missing one fails the build rather than shipping a platform nothing can read. the id becomes a path segment in the signed rules url, so it stays lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. imageHosts names the cdn hosts a thumbnail may point at beyond the platform hosts themselves, and anything else is dropped rather than rendered. a locale is an entry here plus a number and date format in extension/src/extract/normalise.ts, and sites.test.ts checks every locale has one so a platform is never read with nobody's number format.

fields.subject: what the platform reviews, product by default. the interface says business where a platform reviews one, since a review describing something else is a different sentence about a shop than about a kettle.
fields.status: supported by default. a draft platform is registered, tested and readable in a development build, and is stripped from the production manifest, so a platform whose rules are not finished yet never shows a reader a panel that cannot read the page.
fields.pathPrefix: the path the platform lives under, when it does not own its whole host. the content script is matched to that prefix rather than to the host, so a host serving other things is not read.
fields.idCase: upper by default, since an asin is written either way and means the same listing. preserve leaves an id whose case carries meaning alone.
fields.reviewSource: paged-url by default, meaning reviewPath builds a url per page. page-only says the platform has no such url, so verdict reads what the page carries and offers no deeper read.
fields.absentSignals: signals the platform structurally does not record, named so a report says the signal does not exist here rather than that it could not be read. SPEC.md section 6.
